assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and credit cycles gave macroeconomics a tractable account of how credit frictions amplify and propagate shocks. The work underlies the macro-financial models used after 2008 and in current policy analysis. It is conceptually foundational, widely taught and has measurable policy influence.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki–Moore (1997) is the core credit-cycle contribution. Gertler's work with Bernanke and others on the financial accelerator is the complementary strand. Bernanke has already been recognised in 2022, which complicates credit for the accelerator. Gilchrist is an important empirical contributor but is more naturally a fourth name than a core laureate.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of confirmation across theory, quantitative macro and empirical finance. Timing is well supported by the post-2008 recognition of financial frictions.
uncertainties: How the committee would apportion credit between the Kiyotaki–Moore and Bernanke–Gertler strands, given the 2022 prize.
Whether the contribution is judged distinct enough from the 2022 prize on banking and financial crises.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson, Tabellini and Besley systematically brought political institutions, electoral rules, state capacity and fiscal policy into formal economics and empirical testing. They created a major field with a large research programme. The work links closely to recent prizes on institutions and growth.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central figures through their joint book and papers on constitutions and electoral rules. Besley's work on state capacity, with Persson, and on accountability is a strong complement. Credit is clear for Persson and Tabellini. Besley's inclusion is plausible but could be debated.
assessment.maturity: Developed over about 30 years with extensive empirical replication and a broad following. Fully mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity may reduce the perceived novelty of recognising a neighbouring area.
Identification in cross-country constitutional comparisons is contested.
Whether the prize should be limited to two names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection reshaped trade theory and the measurement of trade gains. The Melitz model is now the standard framework in international trade and is widely used in quantitative work. It had a large influence on empirical trade research and policy evaluation.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman supplied the broader monopolistic-competition foundation and, with Melitz and Yeaple, the exporting-versus-FDI extension. Redding is a strong contributor to quantitative spatial and trade applications but is less central to the founding idea. Krugman's 2008 prize covers the earlier new trade theory.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of confirmation. Firm-level data have validated many of the core predictions.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the contribution as sufficiently distinct from Krugman's 2008 prize.
Whether the Eaton–Kortum strand, which is credited to different people on the list, should be paired with it.
Elhanan Helpman is also listed under B029, so credit for his work is divided.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Estimation of demand for differentiated products and of dynamic industry models transformed empirical industrial organisation. It is now standard in merger review, antitrust analysis and many applied fields. The BLP method is among the most widely used structural tools in economics.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (BLP) are clearly credited for the demand estimation method. Pakes also has distinct contributions to dynamic oligopoly (Ericson–Pakes) and to estimation. Bresnahan, Reiss and others made foundational earlier contributions, so selecting only three leaves some disputed credit.
assessment.maturity: Developed over 30 years with extensive use and refinement. Fully mature.
uncertainties: Whether Bresnahan's earlier empirical IO work should share credit.
The list of credited names is large, and the committee would need to justify the limit of three.
Debate remains over how much weight methodological tools receive relative to substantive discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities is the basis of modern monetary policy analysis in central banks. It combines rigorous micro-founded theory with estimable medium-scale models. It has had a large influence on policy practice.
assessment.attribution: This is the hardest attribution problem on the list. It spans Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Gali, Christiano–Eichenbaum–Evans, Smets–Wouters and Gertler, among others. Three names cannot fully capture the contributions. Woodford (theory and policy), Gali (framework) and Christiano (estimated models) are a defensible but arbitrary subset.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with over 25 years of use and refinement. Its record after 2008 and 2021–22 has been tested and sparked renewed debate.
uncertainties: The attribution cut-off is difficult and may leave out equally deserving figures such as Taylor and Calvo.
Persistent questions about the framework's performance in crises and with inflation.
Reliance on a framework that heterogeneous-agent models may partly supersede.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rubinstein's alternating-offers bargaining model is a cornerstone of game theory. It unified strategic and axiomatic bargaining and became the standard microfoundation for bargaining in labour, macro and market models. The extension to markets with search frictions is also widely used.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the primary contributor. Rubinstein–Wolinsky (1985) is the key market extension. Binmore's contributions are important, particularly on the relation of the Nash and Rubinstein solutions, but are secondary on the central result.
assessment.maturity: More than 40 years of confirmation and applications. Fully mature, and arguably overdue relative to its impact.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views game theory as sufficiently recognised by earlier prizes.
Whether Rubinstein alone is the more defensible choice, or whether Wolinsky is needed for the market extension.
Rubinstein's later turn to behavioural and critical work is not central here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Construction of long-run top-income series from tax data created a new empirical foundation for the study of inequality and reshaped public debate. The methodological contribution is substantial. The theoretical interpretation of capital and inequality is more contested.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez (2003) are the central authors of the top-income series. Zucman is a major contributor on offshore wealth and distributional national accounts, but his work is more recent and more debated. Atkinson, who is not on the list, was a key predecessor.
assessment.maturity: The data work has been widely replicated and extended across countries. The interpretation of the dynamics of inequality, and the policy conclusions drawn, remain more disputed.
uncertainties: Debate over the measurement of wealth and capital income, and over the theoretical claims on r>g.
Atkinson's pioneering role cannot be recognised posthumously.
The policy salience of the topic may influence perceptions of scientific merit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hsieh and Klenow showed how misallocation of inputs across firms can quantitatively explain a large part of cross-country differences in income and productivity. This gave the study of development and growth an accessible, widely replicated framework. It has influenced both macro and development research.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) is the core paper. Restuccia and Rogerson's closely related contribution is an important parallel and limits the exclusivity of the credit. Restuccia is on the list, which suggests that a third name is possible.
assessment.maturity: Roughly 15 years of confirmation. It remains highly influential, but the measurement of misallocation continues to be refined and challenged.
uncertainties: Sensitivity of the magnitudes to measurement error and to model assumptions.
Whether Restuccia and Rogerson would share the credit.
Possible concern about the relative immaturity compared with other candidates.
